title: Health and plants: evidence checkpoint
subtitle: Show what you understand, then make one explanation stronger
objective: Apply taught disease, immunity and plant concepts in an original diagnostic checkpoint.

sow.alignment: C39 consolidation of selected previously taught Topic5/6 content. Original16-mark classroom checkpoint after a short recap; not an official exam, grade predictor or a complete Topic5/6 assessment. Record the selected route and support.

priorLearning: Communicable disease, specific immune response and memory.
success: Use causes and mechanisms rather than symptoms alone.
Explain a biological process with correct substances and structures.
Calculate a rate, identify a limitation and improve one answer.

vocabulary.meaning: A feature recognised by the immune system that can trigger a specific response.
A protein that binds to a specific antigen.
A cell supporting a faster later response to a previously encountered antigen.
A measurement used to indicate something else, with limitations.
A task used to identify specific next teaching needs.

equipment: Shared evidence sheet, one selected response route, pen and ruler.
Projector or offline HTML/PowerPoint; calculator where useful.
preparation: Print the shared page, one selected response route and the exit page. Routes are alternatives, not extra tasks.
Read the worked answers and note any constructed data before teaching.
safety: Paper and screen lesson; no human sampling, exercise test, breath holding, medicine handling or personal health disclosure.
practicalAlternative: All evidence is supplied. Use paper diagrams and cards, pointing, annotation or dictation if a device is unavailable.

misconceptions.claim: A symptom proves the disease cause.
misconceptions.correction: Similar symptoms can result from different causes.
misconceptions.check: Use the two supplied cases without guessing a real diagnosis.

misconceptions.correction: Antibodies are proteins; memory lymphocytes are cells.
misconceptions.check: Ask pupils to distinguish the two objects.

misconceptions.correction: Light supplies energy; carbon dioxide and water are the material reactants.

misconceptions.claim: A bubble count is an exact oxygen volume.
misconceptions.correction: Bubble size and dissolved gas limit the proxy.

access.supported: Same core concepts with chunked prompts and read-aloud access. Record support used; a pathway is not a diagnosis or fixed attainment label.
access.standard: Explain the supplied evidence independently using accurate scientific terms and units.
access.stretch: Optional deeper transfer or evaluation. Higher-tier-only material is labelled explicitly and is not required for the core outcome.
access.regulation: Offer solo or partner work, a quiet response, a pass and brief reset with clear re-entry. No forced disclosure or public performance.

slides.title: A checkpoint with a useful next step
body: Use what you have learned, then improve one answer.
This is an original 16-mark classroom task.
slides.notes: Explain formative purpose, route recording and the 17-minute independent window. It is not a prediction of a GCSE grade. Keep pupil marks private.

slides.title: Bring the core distinctions back
body: R1. Does a shared symptom prove a shared cause?
R2. Is a protein a cell?
R3. What must a rate include?
slides.notes: Answers: no; no; amount/change and time with units. Do not reveal the checkpoint data calculations.

slides.title: Read causal evidence
body: I identify the cause before classifying.
A symptom alone is not enough.
slides.notes: Model P communicable because a virus can spread; Q non-communicable because no infectious cause is transmitted. Use these analogous cases, not assessment A/B.

visual.title: A cause test beats a symptom guess
visual.description: Recap comparison: two fictional conditions share a rash symptom. One is caused by a transmissible virus; the other is a non-infectious skin reaction. The cause and route determine the category, not rash alone.

slides.title: Keep the mechanism clear
body: Antigens, antibodies and memory cells have different roles.
A later response is specific to recognised antigen features.
slides.notes: Model one accurate sentence per role. Explain that the recap provides teaching support; checkpoint scores therefore describe post-recap performance.

visual.title: Keep cells and proteins distinct
visual.description: Recap role model linking a recognised antigen to antibody response and retained memory lymphocytes. Memory supports a faster later response to the same antigen; it is not an antibody protein.

slides.title: Calculate, then attach the unit
body: Find the mean count.
Divide by the duration of each count.
slides.notes: Use 7, 8, 9 over 2 minutes: mean 8; rate 4 bubbles/min. Check that pupils see two different divisions with different purposes.

visual.title: Worked method, different numbers
visual.description: Analogous warm-up: three counts each lasting 2 minutes are 7, 8 and 9 bubbles; mean 8 per 2 minutes gives 4 bubbles/min. The checkpoint uses different data.

elements.text: Worked method, different numbers

Counts: 7, 8, 9
Each lasted 2 minutes

Mean count=8
Rate = 4 bubbles/min

(7+8+9)÷3=8; then 8 ÷ 2 = 4
Check the time before writing the rate.
Constructed warm-up data; not the checkpoint answers.

slides.title: Repair a worked explanation
body: W1. “P and Q have a rash, so both must be infectious.”
Repair it with one causal clue.
slides.notes: P’s transmissible virus contrasts with Q’s non-infectious cause. Accept a clear comparison without a diagnosis claim.

body: W2. Which label belongs on a protein: antibody or memory lymphocyte?
slides.notes: Antibody. Ask how the memory-cell label should change; it is a cell. This is a warm-up, not the independent answer sheet.

slides.title: Audit a unit
body: W3. A pupil writes 8 bubbles/min for the warm-up.
Which part of the method did they miss?
slides.notes: The 8 count was per 2 minutes; dividing by 2 gives 4 bubbles/min. Do not expose checkpoint 800-lux answer yet.

slides.title: Ready to work independently?
body: Which statement is accurate?
slides.notes: Correct option: mean and rate answer different questions. Briefly re-teach timing if needed; record extra support.

options.text: A mean count and a per-minute rate can differ.
options.feedback: Yes. A count taken over several minutes must be divided by that duration.

options.text: Every mean count is automatically per minute.
options.feedback: Only if the count interval is one minute; check the supplied time.

slides.title: Choose the agreed route
body: Shared evidence + one response page.
Four questions, 4 marks each: 16 in total.
Work independently for 17 minutes.
slides.notes: Read instructions only. A scribe/read-aloud may support access without adding science; record prompts or scientific help. Do not show answers during this window.

slides.title: Independent checkpoint
body: Use the supplied cases and constructed table.
Show calculations and use precise labels.
If stuck, leave a space and move on.
slides.notes: Keep timer optional and discreet. Supported S1–S4, standard M1–M4 or challenge T1–T4 each totals 16 marks. No public competition. Collect a first response before feedback.

slides.title: Feedback after the checkpoint
body: Use the teacher’s item feedback.
Choose one error with the biggest scientific effect.
slides.notes: Now release relevant answers. Mark with the route-specific 16-mark scheme. Do not compare unlike support routes as equal test conditions.

slides.title: Make the correction explain why
body: L1. Improve one answer using a because statement.
Audience asks: “What evidence or mechanism changed it?”
slides.notes: Allow private teacher/TA discussion. Retain first and revised response as evidence of learning; do not inflate the original independent score.

slides.title: Plan the next five minutes of teaching
body: E1. Name one distinction you can now explain.
E2. Choose one next step: cause, memory, plant transport or rate.
slides.notes: Accept a specific accurate distinction and an actionable next step. Scores guide re-teaching by item, not a grade boundary.

slides.title: Keep both versions
body: First attempt shows the starting point.
A reasoned correction shows the improvement.
slides.notes: Shared exit minute. Record route, support and one next teaching target.

pupilPages.title: Shared evidence | Checkpoint cases and measurements
pupilPages.intro: Use these original cases and constructed sample data. No personal health information is needed.

blocks.text: Warm-up only (W1–W3): P has a rash caused by a transmissible virus; Q has a rash from a non-infectious skin reaction. W1: does the same symptom establish the same cause? W2: an antibody is a protein; a memory lymphocyte is a cell. Explain the difference. W3: separate practice counts are 7, 8 and 9 bubbles, each over 2 minutes. Find the mean and then the rate per minute. Use the checkpoint cases below only for the independent task.

cards.title: Case A
cards.text: A fictional respiratory illness is caused by a virus that can pass between hosts. Coughing may occur.

cards.title: Case B
cards.text: An inherited airway condition is not caused by a transmissible infectious agent. Coughing may occur.

blocks.text: Constructed pondweed investigation: same shoot, solution and temperature at both light levels. Each count lasts 3 minutes. Bubble volumes may differ and some oxygen dissolves.

blocks.prompt: Record the route used and any read-aloud, scribing or additional support.

pupilPages.title: Supported route | Four scientific checks
pupilPages.intro: Original 16-mark checkpoint. Use the shared cases and constructed data. Each numbered question is worth 4 marks. Record the route/support; this is not an official exam paper. Access word bank: cause; feature; protein; cell; reactant; tissue; time; proxy.

blocks.prompt: S1. Classify cases A and B as communicable or non-communicable [2]. Give the causal reason for A [1]. Explain why coughing alone cannot decide [1].
S2. Define antigen [1] and antibody [1]. Identify memory lymphocytes as cells [1] and explain their role in a later response to the same antigen [1].
S3. Name both material reactants of photosynthesis [1] and its sugar product [1]. Name the tissue carrying water/mineral ions [1] and the tissue carrying sucrose [1].
S4. For 800 lux, calculate the mean count [1] and bubbles per minute [1]. Name one control for comparing the two light levels [1] and one reason count is not exact oxygen volume [1].

pupilPages.intro: Original 16-mark checkpoint. Use the shared cases and constructed data. Each numbered question is worth 4 marks. Record the route/support; this is not an official exam paper.

blocks.prompt: M1. Classify cases A and B as communicable or non-communicable [2]. Give the causal reason for A [1]. Explain why coughing alone cannot decide [1].

pupilPages.title: Challenge route | Precise explanations
pupilPages.intro: Original 16-mark checkpoint. Use the shared cases and constructed data. Each numbered question is worth 4 marks. Record the route/support; this is not an official exam paper. Answer without the access word bank; justify each causal or measurement distinction.

blocks.prompt: T1. Classify cases A and B as communicable or non-communicable [2]. Give the causal reason for A [1]. Explain why coughing alone cannot decide [1].
T2. Define antigen [1] and antibody [1]. Identify memory lymphocytes as cells [1] and explain their role in a later response to the same antigen [1].
T3. Name both material reactants of photosynthesis [1] and its sugar product [1]. Name the tissue carrying water/mineral ions [1] and the tissue carrying sucrose [1].

pupilPages.title: Feedback and next step | Keep first and revised answers
pupilPages.intro: Complete this after the independent checkpoint. Corrections are not added to the first-attempt score.

blocks.prompt: L1. Copy one short part of your first answer. Improve it and explain why the change is scientifically stronger.
E1. State one distinction you can now explain accurately.
E2. Choose one specific next teaching target and say what would help.

choices: Separate antibody proteins and memory cells.
Calculate a rate and state its proxy limit.

answers.label: Retrieval and warm-up
answers.answer: R1: no; R2: no; R3: amount/change per time with units. W1: P communicable/Q non-communicable because causes differ. W2: antibody protein; memory lymphocyte cell. W3: mean 8 is per 2 minutes; rate 4 bubbles/min. Hinge: mean and rate may differ.

answers.label: S1 / M1 / T1 — 4 marks
answers.answer: 1 mark: A communicable; 1 mark: B non-communicable; 1 mark: A has a transmissible viral cause; 1 mark: similar symptoms can have different causes. Do not credit an unsupported diagnosis.

answers.label: S2 / M2 / T2 — 4 marks
answers.answer: 1 mark: antigen is a recognised molecular feature triggering a specific response; 1 mark: antibody is a specific binding protein; 1 mark: memory lymphocyte is a cell; 1 mark: memory supports a faster later response to the same antigen. Accept equivalent accurate wording.

answers.label: S3 / M3 / T3 — 4 marks
answers.answer: 1 mark for both carbon dioxide and water; 1 mark: glucose; 1 mark: xylem for water/mineral ions; 1 mark: phloem for sucrose. Light is energy, not a material reactant; no credit for light replacing either reactant.

answers.label: S4 / M4 / T4 — 4 marks
answers.answer: 1 mark: (30+33+36)/3=33 bubbles; 1 mark: 33/3=11 bubbles/min; 1 mark: valid control such as same shoot/solution/temperature/count duration; 1 mark: bubble sizes differ or oxygen dissolves. If an incorrect mean is carried forward, award rate-method mark for correctly dividing that mean by 3 with the correct unit.

answers.label: L1 and exit
answers.answer: L1: credit a specific corrected explanation with reason, recorded separately from first score. E1: any accurate taught distinction. E2: actionable item-level target. A score alone is not sufficient diagnostic feedback.

answers.label: Assessment record
answers.answer: Total 16 marks per route. Record route, read-aloud/scribe support and any scientific prompting. Do not assign official grades or claim qualification evidence completion. Re-teach: Q1 cause/route; Q2 cell/protein/memory; Q3 reactants/tissues; Q4 mean versus rate/proxy.

teacherNotes: 40-minute lesson. Zero-minute slides share the preceding stage allocation.
Choose one response route. Accept accurate speech, pointing with explanation, annotations or writing; record the support used.
A teacher or TA can be a quiet audience: ask one evidence question, then let the pupil revise or justify a decision.
Suggested timing: opening 2, retrieval 2, I do7, We do4, hinge 1, independent 18 including instructions, feedback 5, exit 1. The independent response window is 17 minutes.

All routes use the same core items and 16-mark scheme; supported wording/word bank changes access. Record that difference and any additional prompting rather than treating scores as standardised comparisons.
Interactive warm-up is restricted to analogous rash cases, role labels and 7/8/9 counts over 2 minutes. It contains none of the assessment’s constructed 800-lux calculation answers.
